messages:
maya: heads-up — after the driver+cuda push this morning ~8 dedicated hosts in ap-southeast are showing intermittent NVLINK/timeout errors and ~10% of small inference jobs fail with `cuInit`/context errors. Not all of them, seems correlated with older custom AMI build. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: alert: gpu-fleet-ap-southeast instance-health spike detected (8 hosts) — increased OOM/NVLINK errors, autoremoved 3 hosts from LB.
samir: quick check: can someone run `uname -r` + `modinfo nvidia` on the affected hosts? my hunch is a kmod mismatch between AMI kernel and the new driver package. seen that before with hotpatches.
maya: running on one now — kernel `5.15.0-1088-aws`, modinfo shows driver 535.54 but the installed dkms/packaging on AMI expects 530 series. copy/paste: ```$ modinfo nvidia | grep version
version: 535.54.03
$ cat /etc/os-release 
NAME="Ubuntu" VERSION="22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)```
jordan: yep that matches mismatch. For dedicated pools we use customer AMIs that sometimes lag kernel patches. If we force driver 535 on older kernels we get subtle nvlink liveness faults. rolling a hotpatch that forces fallback causes perf regression. tradeoffs: rollback drivers -> restores stability but may increase per-token latency by ~6-8% on h100 workloads.
lin: capacity note — we have limited spare dedicated capacity in ap-southeast; moving traffic to other regions will bust reserved capacity SLAs for a few customers unless we use burst pool (which costs extra). we should coordinate with sales if we need to burst.
nana: QA repro notes (small script): ```python
# repro: allocate 8GB tensor on GPU then run small warmup multiprocess
import torch, multiprocessing as mp
def p():
    a = torch.randn(1024,1024, device='cuda')
    for _ in range(100): a += a*0.001
mp.Process(target=p).start()
```
on affected hosts this finishes; affected hit `RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (3): initialization error` after a few iterations.
samir: plan suggestion: 1) pull the 8 affected hosts out of rotation (they're currently autoremoved), 2) boot a canary of 6 hosts with AMI rebuilt to pin kernel+driver combos (downgrade driver to 530 package matching AMI), 3) test heavy KV cache + multi-session workloads, 4) if green, roll by waves of 10% of ap-southeast dedicated pool.
maya: agree. also we should publish a rollback playbook for customers on reserved capacity (so SRE/sales know. include script to repro + quick mitigation: reboot + revert driver package).
jordan: toggle: if we roll back drivers on the whole region we may see increased unit-cost (fewer tokens/sec) and risk violating latency SLOs for some premium customers. recommend canary + 2-hour soak and metric check: 99th p95 latency, scheduler queue length, and job fail rate.
deploy-bot: scheduled action: canary wave start at 1876543500 (in 3m) — rolling 6 hosts with ami:rdw-dedicated-2026-05-12-530. ops-bot: noted. tagging owners: @samir @maya @lin.
nana: QA will run the regression suite on canary once up — ETA 20m after deployed.
samir: if canary fails, immediate rollback step: `ansible -i canary_hosts.yml -m shell -a "apt install --allow-downgrades nvidia-driver-530 -y && reboot"` and mark images with `broken-driver-535` tag to prevent future auto-rolls.
maya: also file a follow-up to update our AMI build pipeline to validate kernel+driver combos (CI integration) and add a pre-roll driver check in rollout pipeline. filing ticket now. :memo:
nana: QA: +1 for CI test — will add param matrix to nightly. :thumbsup:
jordan: final call: keep dedicated pool drains manual until we confirm canary. if we need burst capacity coordinate with @sales for short-term credits.
maya: thanks all — I'll own the on-call handoff and run the rollback playbook if canary fails. ping me in thread with logs. :eyes:
